title: Try the OSC adapter against a real console
notes: On 2026-10-28 `core/osc_console.c` joined QLC+ as a second adapter (`dmxdesk --osc FILE`), proven on loopback and in `--qt-pipe` mode against a UDP socket playing the console: the Vibra gesture script sends the same controls in the same order as over QLC+, with the same 41 controls enabled. No real OSC console has received it yet, and the press-as-1-then-0 and the 0..1 grand master are the common convention, not any one console's. Next: write a surface file for one console that speaks OSC (QLC+'s own OSC input plugin on the headless engine at :9997 needs no venue hardware) and check each kind of control moves there.
result: QLC+ 5.2.2's OSC input on loopback drives buttons, solo frames, flashes, stop-all, dial time and multipliers through the adapter, with QLC+'s feedback heard; msRange, factorAddresses and per-item feedback added for what it needed; hidden-page widgets documented as disabled
evidence: 9efe979. Trial on a headless QLC+ on :9996 with the Vibra workspace mapped to /vibra/<id>: toggle/solo/flash/stop states and feedback events match, dial 504->501 ms, 700->698 ms, factors 1/16x..16x set; host suite 59/59, ARM -Werror clean
